assumptions.statement: Official regulatory controls, ownership, existing buildings, municipal utilities, fire access and engineering constraints are unavailable.
assumptions.impact: FAR, building density, height, demolition, utilities and statutory implementation remain unknown; the proposal offers only conceptual design moves.

assumptions.statement: The overall and three key-area polygons are the repository provisional intake geometry derived from public text and area constraints.
assumptions.impact: All geometry-sensitive areas and ratios must be regenerated when organizer-supplied official polygons arrive.

assumptions.statement: No official road redlines, station exits, lift status feeds or verified barrier-free network are present.
assumptions.impact: Road area and real accessible-route performance remain unknown; road lines are conceptual service links only.

assumptions.statement: No field trial, interview, user test, robot deployment or live public-service integration was authorized or performed.
assumptions.impact: Scenario performance is unproven; every pilot starts with baseline collection, consent, stop rules and human ownership.

assumptions.statement: The Barrier-Free Environment Law Article 39 human-service requirement is cited only for the listed medical, social-security, financial and living-payment services.
assumptions.impact: The broader dual-path protocol is a voluntary design proposal, not a claim that every urban interface has the same statutory duty.
